conjectures: This graph is now closed as a source of forced-equal distinct pairs at k>=5. The geometry branch's amplifier needs such a pair, so it needs a different seed: a graph with fewer 5-colourings, which in practice means one with a smaller independent set structure around the target pair, or the same region at k=4 where the colourings are far more constrained.

Forced equalities are more plentiful at lower k, and the certificate technique transfers: at k=4 the survivor set of this graph will be nonempty (indeed each diamond forces equality at k=3), so the same pipeline should be run at k=4 to extract candidate forced-equal pairs with exact d^2, which is exactly the input the amplifier needs.

The class-refinement schedule is efficient here because 24 signature classes concentrated the difficulty: the largest class of 19 vertices accounted for 171 of the 491 pairs and the first target removed 111. Class size is therefore a good proxy for target value, and the same schedule should be reused on any new seed graph.

escalation.obstacle: Supply a genuine forced-equal DISTINCT pair to the geometry branch's finite amplifier. This graph provably has none at k>=5, so the amplifier needs either a different unit-distance seed or the same seed at k=4, where the question is open.
escalation.definitions: A unit-distance graph is a finite graph with an injection into R^2 such that uv is an edge iff |u-v| = 1. Proper k-colouring: c(u) != c(v) on every edge. A pair is forced equal at k if G is k-colourable and G plus the edge pq is not; the added edge is a combinatorial disequality constraint, and for a survivor pair |p-q| != 1, so it is never a unit edge. Coordinates in Q(sqrt3, sqrt5, sqrt11), basis [1,3,5,11,15,33,55,165].
escalation.hypotheses: Exact real-algebraic coordinates; complete finite graph; threshold k = 4 or 5; no measurability, periodicity or lattice hypothesis.
escalation.attempted_approaches: Single-pair probe (SAT); block-one-partition ensemble of 8 (344 eliminations); static 8-pair chase (3458 eliminations, 491 left); adaptive class-refinement chase of 16 targets (491 -> 0 in 0.23 s), yielding the no-forcing certificate at k>=5; Theorems A and B ruling out the direct common-neighbour mechanism for k >= 4.
escalation.expected_useful_output: Either a forced-equal distinct pair from the k=4 run of the same pipeline, reported with exact coordinates and d^2 and with the separating-witness certificate that justifies the claim (or a solver-only candidate if UNSAT cannot be certified in budget), or a second no-forcing certificate at k=4 which would show that even at four colours this point set forces no equality, in which case the seed itself must be replaced and the graph family, not the witness schedule, is the thing to vary.
